_note: SAMPLE. Generated from the hypothesised draft so the pages can be built and reviewed before Thursday. Replaced by live data on draft day.

roast.text: Best player on the board, top quarterback in a superflex league, taken at three. Zero better players available, zero reaches, nothing to work with. Keshia has accidentally done everything right, and we will not be telling her.

Three of the last five picks were running backs, so Jay looked at the board and took the running back. National ADP had Jonathan Taylor at 6.33 and he went sixth. Somewhere a projection model is quietly asking why anyone needed Jay for this.

Amon-Ra St. Brown at ten, one and a half slots later than the rest of America was taking him, with nobody better on the board. No reach, no gap, no crime. The Substation Superstars have committed a competent act, which we are logging as an outlier.

James Cook III was sitting right there at rank 11 and Mike went Jalen Hurts six slots ahead of value. De'Von Achane and Drake Maye also declined to be taken. The rest of the country had Hurts going 54th, which is the sort of thing you learn in January.

James Cook III, the highest-ranked player left, one slot after the board said. Evan waited for the safe answer to fall into his lap and then took it. The team name still says "Waiting to draft," which is somehow the boldest thing about this.

For Chris Olave at 20 to work, thirty better players have to be wrong, Breece Hall has to disappoint, and rank 50 has to have been a typo. Three things, all load-bearing. Bree needs every one of them.

Ashton Jeanty was on the board at rank 22 and Jesse took Travis Etienne Jr., ranked 37, thirteen slots early. Jeremiyah Love and CeeDee Lamb also went unbothered. Even standard ADP had Etienne almost eighteen picks later than this.

Nico Collins is expected to lead the Texans receiving corps after Jayden Higgins's season-ending ACL tear, which is a real reason to like him and not a reason to take him twenty slots early. CeeDee Lamb, ranked 24, watched the whole thing happen. Da Reigning Champ is defending the title with a depth chart note.

Patrick Mahomes, four slots after the board said, in the middle of a quarterback run three deep. Nobody better was available and Evan took the name everyone knows. He is listed as questionable, which is the only interesting thing in the sentence.

That is four quarterbacks. Zero receivers, two running backs, four quarterbacks, and superflex only starts two of them. Jaxson Dart is part of a Giants trio with Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers that played 18 snaps together in 2025, and Mike is building the roster equivalent of that number.

Eighteen better players have to be mispriced, Justin Herbert at rank 38 has to be a rounding error, and Tetairoa McMillan has to outrun his own rank of 59 by eighteen slots. Colin needs all three to land. Drake London and Caleb Williams sat there and quietly declined to help.

Jared Goff, seven slots after the board said, with literally nobody better left on it. The third quarterback in five picks and somehow the correct one. Keshia now has four quarterbacks and one running back, which suggests the process was not what produced this.

DJ Moore at 55 with twenty-nine better players unclaimed, one of them Jordan Love at rank 54. Garrett Wilson and George Pickens were also available for the same price. Twenty-nine slots early is not a lean, it is a fall.

Harold Fannin Jr. joins a roster that already had a tight end, taken eleven slots before rank 69 said to. George Pickens at 56 was there, so were Davante Adams and Zay Flowers. Justin is stacking positions instead of value, which is a collection, not a roster.

Twenty-five slots early, and standard ADP had Tony Pollard going twenty-five picks later too, so nobody anywhere was doing this. Zay Flowers at rank 58, DeVonta Smith and George Kittle all stayed on the board. That is a fourth running back on a team with one quarterback.

George Kittle, rank 63, was the best thing on the board and Bree took Sam Darnold eleven slots ahead of rank 79. Tyler Shough and Bucky Irving were part of the same discount bin. America had Darnold going 162nd, which is a fact best left sitting there.

Best player available, seven slots after the board said, and it is a fifth running back. Count the shape: one quarterback, five running backs, one receiver. Doug is drafting a backfield and hoping the rest of the lineup fills itself in.

For this to work DK Metcalf has to beat his rank of 97 by twenty-one slots, Sam LaPorta at 68 has to have been overrated, and the questionable tag has to mean nothing. Rome Odunze and Tee Higgins were the cheaper versions of the same bet. Chenell needs the whole stack to hold.

Five receivers. Two quarterbacks, zero running backs, zero tight ends, five receivers. Rome Odunze at rank 70 was right there and Tyler went and got another one of the thing he already has too many of.

This is a pick for a version of Luther Burden III that has not shown up yet, taken eleven slots before rank 92 and with Rome Odunze at 70 still sitting there. He is listed as questionable and suffered a groin injury on 8 August in a contested red-zone rep. James is buying the highlight reel he imagined.

Odunze at 82, twelve slots after rank 70 said he should have gone, with nothing better left on the board. Justin waited, took value, and balanced a roster that now reads 2 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 TE. We will file this under things that happened to him rather than things he did.

Third receiver off the board in five picks and Mike stepped politely into the queue for the last one. Tee Higgins was the safest name available, listed questionable, and the entire country had him at 51. Nobody has ever been fired for this pick, which is exactly the problem.

Eighth round opens and Evan adds a fourth running back to a team with one quarterback. Rhamondre Stevenson started 13 of 14 games last season and still got out-touched by TreVeyon Henderson, 25.1 percent to 18.9. Two quarterback slots start every week, and Evan is furnishing the other rooms.

The other half of the New England committee, four picks later. Henderson held a 25.1 percent touch share to Stevenson's 18.9 last season, which is a lead in the way a nose is a lead. James is now the proud owner of one quarterback and a fourth running back.

Mark Andrews went 82nd on the board and 89th here, while the rest of America was waiting until pick 126. Colin found 37 slots of value and did it with a straight face. Correct, patient, and completely unlike him, so we will call it weather rather than skill.

Three tight ends, three receivers, and now a second running back. What Bree's roster does not have is a second quarterback, in a format that starts two. Rico Dowdle is a fine pick to make while the actual hole in the lineup keeps getting deeper.

Chenell already had DK Metcalf and has now added the Steelers' other guy. Jaylen Warren makes it four running backs, three receivers, and still no quarterback at all. Matching jerseys is a look, not a lineup.

Isaiah Likely sat at rank 102 and Jay took Marvin Harrison Jr. at 105 instead. Christian Watson and Hunter Henry were also on the board for the same price. A fifth receiver for a team with one quarterback and a single tight end.

Twenty-six better players were available and James went and got Michael Wilson to sit alongside Marvin Harrison Jr. T.J. Hockenson and Christian Watson, rank 103, both stayed put. Two Cardinals receivers is not a plan, it is season-ticket behaviour.

Round ten, and the quarterback count is still one. Xavier Worthy makes six receivers while Josh Jacobs, Michael Pittman Jr. and Aaron Jones Sr. at rank 111 all went unclaimed. At some point the second starting slot is going to want an occupant.

Best player on the board, taken five slots after his rank, with nobody better left behind. Bree got it exactly right, which after three tight ends and one quarterback reads less like a plan and more like a slip of the mouse. We will let her have this one and pretend it was intentional.

Pittman makes four receivers for a roster that still has exactly one quarterback, and the rest of America was taking him 90th. Chenell paid 117 for the privilege and got the best name left on the board doing it. Competence this specific, on a team shaped this badly, has to be an accident.

Diggs joins Mike Evans' old address in Doug's collection, because two Buccaneers receivers is apparently the vision. Eighteen better players were sitting there, including Josh Jacobs at rank 115, and Doug reached past all of them to complete the set. Six running backs and two receivers is not a lineup, it is a gift shop.

Count it: three quarterbacks, five running backs, two receivers, zero tight ends. Jesse has now solved the same problem five times and left two starting spots as a rumour. Jacobs was genuinely the best player left, which somehow makes the shape worse.

That is a seventh running back for a team with two receivers, and Rachaad White arrives to keep Stefon Diggs company in Doug's Tampa Bay wing. Kenny Gainwell at rank 118 was right there, along with nine other better players. The jerseys match beautifully and the starting lineup does not exist.

Five running backs, four receivers, a tight end, and one quarterback in a format that starts two. Gainwell was the best player available, so this was the correct answer to a question Chenell should have stopped asking six picks ago. The second slot is not going to fill itself in round twelve.

The rest of the country waits until 136 for Croskey-Merritt and Bree took him at 125 with nobody better on the board. Two clean picks in a row now, which for a roster carrying three tight ends and one quarterback is statistically improbable. Somebody check whether she has been replaced.

Engram was ranked 157th here and 170th nationally, and Jay called his name at 126. Terrance Ferguson at rank 121, Blake Corum and Brian Thomas Jr. all stayed on the board while this happened. Thirty-one better players is not a hunch, it is a decision nobody else in America would have signed.

Brian Thomas Jr. was sitting at rank 123 and James took MarShawn Lloyd, rank 152, instead. Jakobi Meyers and Aaron Rodgers were also available, and one of those would have addressed the single quarterback on the roster. Twenty-four better players, third running back in five picks, no explanation offered.

Justin already has five receivers and has now spent 130 on a sixth, which is a strange way to hedge against your own roster. Brian Thomas Jr. was the best player left, so the value is real even if the need is imaginary. Two running backs, though. Two.

Six receivers, four running backs, one tight end, one quarterback. Addison was genuinely the best name left, which is the only reason this reads as a pick rather than a symptom. The shape of that roster starts two quarterbacks and owns one.

Jeudy was ranked 163rd here and the country had him at 168, and Colin called it at 137. Twenty-six better players stayed on the board, Quentin Johnston and Cam Ward among them. That is not a market inefficiency, that is Colin bidding against nobody and winning.

Quentin Johnston sat at rank 134 and Tyler went past him for Wan'Dale Robinson, listed questionable. Cam Ward and Khalil Shakir were also there, and the roster has one running back and six receivers. Four better players, and he chose the seventh wideout.

One quarterback. Twelve rounds in, six receivers deep, and Ridley makes seven pass-catchers for a lineup that needs two starting passers. Cam Ward was available at this exact moment, which is the part Jay will want to forget by September.

Shakir was the best player on the board and Keshia took him a shade after his rank, which is fine. What is not fine is the five quarterbacks stacked behind him. Two receivers, five quarterbacks, and only two of those quarterbacks can play at once.

Nailor at 143 with a league rank of 172 and a national number of 171. Twenty-nine better players stayed put, including Gunnar Helm at 138, which matters when your roster is seven running backs and three receivers with no tight end. Nobody in the country was taking this pick within thirty slots of here.

Chris Godwin Jr. was sitting at rank 147 and James took a tight end ranked 175 instead. Deebo Samuel and KC Concepcion were also on the board. Twenty-two better players, and the quarterback column still reads one.

Deebo makes five receivers to go with three tight ends, three running backs and two quarterbacks. Eight pass-catchers for a lineup that cannot start eight. The pick itself was the best available, which is the cruel part.

A Denver defense at 157, with Romeo Doubs at rank 150 and RJ Harvey and Zach Charbonnet all still there. This one carried a league rank of 947, so Evan jumped 790 places to get it. First defense off the board and it was not close to necessary.

The Seahawks defense goes to a roster that has started one quarterback all draft in a two-quarterback format. Seven hundred and ninety-one better players were available, Romeo Doubs at rank 150 among them. James has now spent round fourteen protecting himself from points he was never going to score.

Four defenses have gone in the last five picks and Colin made sure he was not left out. Romeo Doubs, rank 150, watched him take a unit ranked 952 instead. That is 791 better players declined for the privilege of being fifth in a run nobody needed to join.

Two starting quarterback slots. Jay has filled one of them, and he has now spent a pick on the Lions defense to make sure the other stays empty a little longer. RJ Harvey and Zach Charbonnet were there; so, presumably, were quarterbacks.

Romeo Doubs, rank 150, still on the board. Bree took a defense ranked 959 with 795 better players available, which is the kind of number that stops being a mistake and starts being a decision. The Eagles will be fine. The roster is a separate question.

Jesse already had six running backs and a single tight end, so naturally the gap he identified was Los Angeles. The Chargers defense joins the collection at 801 spots ahead of its rank, with Romeo Doubs left behind. Rosters have positions; this one has a favourite city.

For this to pay off, Brandon Aubrey has to be the best kicker in football, kickers have to swing weeks, and the 790 players Jesse skipped have to all bust. Three things, and the third one includes Romeo Doubs at rank 150. The rest of the country waited until 85 on average; Jesse could not.

Cameron Dicker at 170 with a league rank of 954, while Romeo Doubs sat at 150 and RJ Harvey and Zach Charbonnet went untouched. Doug has seven running backs and now a kicker listed questionable. Seven hundred and ninety better players, and he went shopping for field goals.

Jason Myers works out if Seattle scores just enough to reach the red zone and not enough to finish, if 790 better players underdeliver, and if Romeo Doubs at 150 turns out to be nothing. Chenell needs all three, and the third one is the load-bearing wall. Nationally he goes at 116, which is its own indictment.

Round fifteen, and the quarterback column on Bree's roster still reads one in a format that starts two. Four tight ends, four receivers, four backs, and now Ka'imi Fairbairn at 785 slots ahead of his rank. The kicker cannot take a snap, but at this stage neither can anyone else on the bench.

Eddy Pineiro carries a league rank of 960 and Romeo Doubs was sitting at 150 the whole time. RJ Harvey and Zach Charbonnet too, both untouched, both better than a kicker taken 786 spots early. Jay now has six receivers, one kicker and a lineup problem he keeps declining to solve.

One quarterback, six receivers, and the fifteenth-round answer was Jake Bates. The format has asked for a second starting passer since the first pick of the draft, and James has responded with a defense and a kicker in consecutive rounds. Romeo Doubs, rank 150, is still available and would also not have been a quarterback, but he would at least have been good.
